title: Nephi Returns to Zarahemla
summary: After preaching and prophesying among the people in the land northward, Nephi returns to the land of his nativity because they reject his words.

explicit_facts.text: In the sixty and ninth year of the judges, Nephi returned from the land northward to the land of Zarahemla.
Nephi had preached the word of God and prophesied among the people in the land northward.
The people rejected Nephi's words, and he returned to the land of his nativity.

unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, clothing, travel method, and route are not stated.

narration.text: Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned to the land of Zarahemla

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the northern people or a preaching event as present; the verses summarize these earlier events.

title: Nephi Sees the Corruption
summary: Nephi sees the people's wickedness and Gadianton robbers occupying judgment-seats and positions of government; sorrow overwhelms him.

explicit_facts.text: Gadianton robbers filled the judgment-seats, usurped power and authority, and did no justice.
The righteous were condemned while the guilty and wicked went unpunished because of money; officials ruled for gain and glory and did as they pleased.
Nephi saw the iniquity among the Nephites and felt great sorrow.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi witnesses the effects of corrupt rule and appears sorrowful.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, court, and government setting are not specifically located or described.

narration.text: his heart was swollen with sorrow within his breast

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verses 4–5 report wrongdoing; they do not narrate each crime as a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage murders, thefts, adultery, or specific trials as events occurring in this moment.

title: Nephi's Sorrow
summary: Seeing the iniquity that had come upon the Nephites, Nephi exclaims in sorrow. He wishes he had lived in earlier days, then acknowledges the sorrow of his own days.

explicit_facts.text: Great iniquity had come upon the Nephites in the space of not many years.
When Nephi saw it, he felt sorrow and exclaimed in agony.
Nephi wishes he had lived when his father Nephi first came out of Jerusalem.
Nephi says he would have had joy in his brethren's righteousness in those days.
Nephi says he is filled with sorrow because of his brethren's wickedness in his own days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may appear sorrowful while speaking.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, posture, and surroundings are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, I am consigned that these are my days, and that my soul shall be filled with sorrow because of this the wickedness of my brethren.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier generation as physically present.

title: Nephi Bows on His Tower
summary: In his garden in Zarahemla, Nephi bows on a tower near the garden gate and highway, pouring out his soul to God. Passersby see him and tell the people.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi's garden tower was by the highway leading to the chief market in Zarahemla and near the garden gate.
Nephi bowed on the tower and poured out his soul to God.
Certain men passing by saw Nephi; they ran and told the people what they had seen.

title: Warning About Their Hearts
summary: Nephi rebukes the people for yielding to temptation and hardening their hearts, urging them to repent and turn to the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the people have given the devil great hold upon their hearts.
He warns that temptation seeks to bring their souls to everlasting misery and endless woe.
Nephi calls them to repent and turn to the Lord their God.
He says they have hardened their hearts, refused to heed the good shepherd, and provoked him to anger.

title: Warning and Rebuke
summary: Nephi warns the gathered multitudes that they will be scattered unless they repent, asks how they have forgotten God, and rebukes their pursuit of gain and riches.

Nephi asks how they could have forgotten God on the day he delivered them.
Nephi says they seek gain, praise, gold, and silver, and accuses them of murder, plunder, theft, false witness, and other iniquity.

title: A Warning to Repent
summary: Nephi warns his brethren that unless they repent, woe will come. He says that if they do not repent, their cities will be taken away and the Lord will not grant them strength to withstand their enemies. He says it will be better for the Lamanites than for them unless they repent.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi warns that woe will come to his audience unless they repent.
Nephi warns that if his audience does not repent, their great city and the surrounding great cities will be taken away, leaving them no place in those cities.
Nephi warns that if his audience does not repent, the Lord will not grant them the strength to withstand their enemies that he has granted before.
Nephi says the Lord will not show his strength to the wicked, except to those who repent and hearken to his words.
Nephi says it will be better for the Lamanites than for his audience unless the audience repents.

Nephi says the Lamanites are more righteous because they have not sinned against the great knowledge his audience received. He says the Lord will be merciful to the Lamanites, lengthen their days, and increase their seed, while his audience will be utterly destroyed unless it repents.

title: Condemnation of the Secret Band
summary: Nephi condemns the people's alliance with Gadianton's secret band, pride, wickedness, and abominations. He warns of destruction unless they repent and testifies that the Lord made these things known to him.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says the people united themselves to the secret band established by Gadianton.
He condemns their pride, riches, wickedness, and abominations.
He warns that unless they repent, they will perish, lose their lands, and be destroyed from the earth.
Nephi says the Lord God made these things known to him and he testifies that they will happen.
